name: Bioptimus
product: Builds multimodal foundation models spanning biological scales, beginning with digital pathology and spatial biology.
targetCustomer: Pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics and life-sciences R&D teams
buyer: Head of computational biology or discovery R&D
traction: H-Optimus-0 was publicly released in 2024; the company cites independent HEST and University of Leeds evaluations, but commercial adoption and revenue are not disclosed.
notes: The $41M injection was not labeled Series A, so stage remains Seed. Strong research and data-access thesis; monetization is earlier than model validation. Dedupe watch: life-sciences/foundation-model missions; canonical domain bioptimus.com.

name: Probabl
product: Commercializes enterprise tooling and support around scikit-learn, including the Skore model-development and evaluation framework.
targetCustomer: Data-science and machine-learning teams
buyer: Head of data science or ML platform
traction: Inria reported more than 2.5B scikit-learn downloads; this is ecosystem distribution, not Probabl product revenue.
notes: Defensibility comes from stewardship, trust and distribution around scikit-learn rather than exclusive model IP. Dedupe watch: data/developer-tool mission; canonical domain probabl.ai.

sources.label: Inria on Probabl and €18.5M seed funding

name: Gladia
product: Provides real-time multilingual speech-to-text and audio-intelligence APIs with diarization, translation and summarization.
targetCustomer: Software companies embedding voice and audio intelligence
buyer: VP Engineering or product lead
traction: OVHcloud reported more than 300,000 developers and 2,000 enterprise customers in June 2026 across more than 100 languages.
notes: OVH Groupe entered exclusive acquisition negotiations on 2026-06-11; the transaction was publicly pending at the research cutoff, so Gladia remains included but should be rechecked before merge. Dedupe watch: speech/infrastructure missions.

name: Photoroom
product: Automates product-image creation and editing across mobile, web and API for sellers, brands and marketplaces.
targetCustomer: SMBs, marketplaces, e-commerce brands and creative teams
buyer: Head of e-commerce or creative operations
traction: The company reported more than 300M downloads across 180+ countries and more than 7B images processed annually in 2026.
notes: Not a thin wrapper: proprietary vision models, product-specific workflow and consumer-to-enterprise distribution are the core advantages. Usage metrics are company-reported.

name: Twin
product: Lets users assemble and run browser-based agents that execute repeatable operational workflows across third-party tools.
targetCustomer: SMBs and operations teams automating browser workflows
buyer: COO or operations lead
traction: Twin reported more than 100,000 agents deployed during a one-month beta; paid usage, retention and revenue were not disclosed.
notes: Explicit weak-wrapper comparator: public evidence shows orchestration and UX on top of third-party models and tools, but no proprietary model or durable data moat yet. Canonical legal entity is Twin Labs SAS.

name: LightOn
subsector: Private generative AI and document intelligence
product: Provides the Paradigm enterprise generative-AI platform for private document search, assistants and workflow automation.
targetCustomer: Regulated enterprises and public-sector organizations
buyer: CIO, CDO or CISO
fundingDisplay: €11.9M gross IPO proceeds; prior private funding not consolidated
traction: LightOn disclosed an enterprise deployment across more than 450 Sodern employees; contract value and broader ARR were not disclosed.
notes: Technically deeper than a generic RAG wrapper because of its research/model history and private deployment stack; commercial moat still depends on regulated workflow adoption. Public-company status is unusual for this cohort.

sources.label: LightOn product and company media kit

name: Kili Technology
product: Provides collaborative annotation, data curation and evaluation workflows for image, video, text, audio and geospatial AI datasets.
targetCustomer: Enterprise AI, ML and data-operations teams
buyer: Head of AI, ML platform or data operations
fundingDisplay: $32M across a $7M seed and $25M Series A
traction: Kili says its platform went live in 2020 and early customers renewed; current customer count, ARR and retention are not publicly disclosed.
notes: Workflow and integration depth matter, but Kili does not own customer training data and operates in a crowded annotation/evaluation market. Dedupe watch: data tooling mission; canonical domain kili-technology.com.

name: SiPearl
product: Designs Rhea1, a sovereign European Arm-based CPU for exascale HPC and AI systems with high-bandwidth memory.
targetCustomer: Supercomputing centers, sovereign cloud providers and HPC system OEMs
buyer: HPC system architect or public-compute procurement lead
fundingDisplay: €130M Series A plus €7.4M EU launch grant; instruments include equity and convertible financing
traction: SiPearl reported first Rhea1 power-on in May 2026 and schedules general availability for end-2026; JUPITER is the publicly named lead deployment.
notes: Deep hardware and sovereignty moat, but execution risk remains high until volume availability and system-level performance are demonstrated. A Series B launch was announced, not a completed financing. Dedupe watch: semiconductor mission.

name: VSORA
product: Designs Jotunn8, a data-center inference accelerator targeting high-throughput transformer and generative-AI workloads.
targetCustomer: AI server OEMs, cloud providers and data-center operators
buyer: AI infrastructure architect or OEM product lead
fundingDisplay: $46M latest venture round; cumulative funding not verified
latestRound: $46M venture round, 2025; round label not disclosed
traction: VSORA announced Jotunn8 tape-out in October 2025; no independent silicon benchmark or current general-availability evidence was found.
notes: Promising architecture, but company performance claims are pre-production claims until independently validated. Stage is Unknown because the official financing release did not name the round. Dedupe watch: semiconductor mission.

name: GreenWaves Technologies
product: Designs GAP-series programmable RISC-V SoCs for neural-network and signal-processing workloads in battery-powered devices.
targetCustomer: Hearables, smart-sensor, health-device and IoT OEMs
buyer: Embedded-systems architect or semiconductor procurement lead
fundingDisplay: €20M 2023 financing package; cumulative funding not verified
traction: Bpifrance reported roughly twelve audio and IoT customers in 2023 and production ramp for GAP9; current shipment volume and revenue are not disclosed.
notes: Real chip-plus-toolchain depth and regional differentiation. The €20M announcement mixes equity and other financing, so it is not treated as cumulative equity. Dedupe watch: semiconductor mission.

name: Aqemia
product: Uses generative AI and physics-based simulation to discover small-molecule candidates for partners and an internal therapeutic pipeline.
targetCustomer: Pharmaceutical and biotechnology discovery organizations
buyer: Head of drug discovery or business development
latestRound: $38M venture round, 2024; round label not disclosed
traction: Aqemia disclosed a multi-year Sanofi collaboration with up to $140M in potential payments and multiple internally generated programs; milestone value is contingent, not recognized revenue.
notes: Technically and vertically integrated beyond a SaaS wrapper, but asset and partner economics remain subject to preclinical and clinical risk. Numeric USD funding is null because the company only states more than $100M. Dedupe watch: drug-discovery mission.

sources.label: Aqemia €60M Series A and Sanofi collaboration

name: Entalpic
product: Combines generative models, graph neural networks and quantum simulations to design catalysts and materials for industrial chemistry.
targetCustomer: Chemical, materials, energy and industrial R&D organizations
buyer: R&D director or head of materials discovery
traction: Entalpic reports a 25-person team and early technical proof points; it announced commercial expansion in 2026, but customers and revenue are not public.
notes: Research depth is high, while vertical integration is still developing: the Grenoble experimental lab is planned, not yet a demonstrated closed loop. Dedupe watch: climate/materials and life-sciences missions.

name: Spore.Bio
product: Combines optical spectroscopy, imaging and machine learning in an instrument for rapid microbial contamination testing.
targetCustomer: Food, cosmetics and pharmaceutical manufacturing quality teams
buyer: Quality director or plant manager
traction: Spore.Bio announced a 30-person team by mid-2025 and a TMSI technology launch in March 2026; installed-base and revenue figures are not public.
notes: Strong device-model-workflow integration and a potential proprietary spectral dataset; regulatory validation and repeatable manufacturing scale remain key risks. Dedupe watch: industrial and life-sciences missions.

name: Gleamer
product: Provides regulated AI tools for X-ray, CT and mammography interpretation integrated into radiology workflows.
targetCustomer: Hospitals, radiology groups and imaging networks
buyer: Chief radiologist, hospital CIO or imaging-network executive
fundingDisplay: €36M disclosed through Series B plus an undisclosed 2025 internal round
traction: Gleamer reported €20M signed ARR at December 2024, more than 2,500 institutions in 49 countries and more than 40M exams processed.
notes: Regulatory approvals, multi-modality portfolio and embedded radiology distribution create stronger defensibility than a single-model application; traction remains first-party reported. Dedupe watch: healthcare/radiology mission.

sources.label: Gleamer company, funding timeline and team

name: Qantev
product: Applies machine learning to health and life insurance claims triage, provider behavior, fraud detection and medical-operations workflows.
targetCustomer: Health and life insurers
buyer: Chief claims officer or medical-operations executive
latestRound: €30M venture round, 2024; round label not disclosed
traction: Qantev reported deployments with AXA, Generali and FWD across 12 countries in 2024; contract value and ARR were not disclosed.
notes: The moat is primarily claims-domain data access, workflow integration and insurer trust rather than a unique foundation model. Stage is Unknown because the official 2024 release did not label the post-Series-A round. Dedupe watch: insurance/fintech mission.

name: Inbolt
product: Uses real-time 3D vision to guide industrial robots and compensate for part-position and production-line variation.
targetCustomer: Automotive, aerospace and industrial manufacturers
buyer: Automation engineering director or plant manager
traction: Inbolt reported production deployment in more than 20 factories in 2024; customer-specific productivity claims were not independently validated.
notes: 3D perception, edge runtime, hardware integration and robot workflow create genuine vertical depth. Scaling across robot brands and factory conditions remains the main execution test.

name: Pelico
product: Provides a supply-chain operations platform that reconciles factory data, flags disruptions and coordinates corrective workflows.
targetCustomer: Complex discrete manufacturers
buyer: Chief supply-chain officer or factory operations leader
traction: Pelico reported 300% year-over-year revenue growth for two consecutive years and deployment across 15 countries at the 2025 financing.
notes: Defensibility is mainly ERP/MES integration, operational data context and workflow embedding; the generative-AI layer itself is unlikely to be the moat. Growth metrics are company-reported.

name: Veesion
product: Analyzes existing retail camera feeds for suspicious gestures and sends real-time alerts to store staff.
targetCustomer: Grocery, pharmacy and specialty-retail store networks
buyer: Head of loss prevention or retail operations
fundingDisplay: €53M total financing, including €38M Series B and €15M non-dilutive financing
traction: Veesion reported more than 5,000 stores in 25 countries and 10% of revenue from the US before opening a local office in 2025.
notes: Large deployed video corpus and tight store workflow are meaningful moats; privacy, false-positive control and retailer concentration are material risks. Funding is not converted to USD because the package mixes dilutive and non-dilutive capital.

name: SESAMm
product: Uses multilingual NLP over public and premium text sources for ESG, reputational, supplier and compliance-risk monitoring.
targetCustomer: Investment firms, banks, insurers and large corporations
buyer: Chief risk officer, head of ESG or investment-data lead
traction: SESAMm currently reports coverage of 30B+ documents, 100+ languages, 5M+ companies and 4M+ public and premium sources.
notes: The moat is the normalized multilingual corpus, entity graph and regulated-risk workflow, not a generic LLM wrapper. Dataset scale is company-reported. Metz legal HQ gives meaningful non-Paris geographic coverage.

name: Synapse Medicine
product: Provides medication decision support, prescription analysis and drug-safety APIs for clinicians, hospitals and digital-health platforms.
targetCustomer: Hospitals, clinicians, public-health bodies and digital-health vendors
buyer: Hospital pharmacy director, chief medical information officer or digital-health product lead
traction: Synapse has deployments with French public-health institutions and hospitals; the company references thousands of healthcare-professional users but does not disclose current ARR.
notes: Clinical knowledge, regulatory integration and prescribing workflow create stronger lock-in than a conversational wrapper. Latest disclosed institutional round is dated, so current financing status should be refreshed at merge. Dedupe watch: healthcare mission.

name: Volta Medical
product: Provides FDA-cleared AI software that analyzes intracardiac electrograms in real time to assist complex atrial-fibrillation ablation procedures.
targetCustomer: Electrophysiology labs and hospitals
buyer: Electrophysiology service chief or hospital procurement lead
traction: Volta obtained FDA clearance for AF-Xplorer in 2023 and announced the first US launch of its GE HealthCare-integrated solution in November 2025.
notes: Regulated clinical workflow, expert-labeled electrogram data and device integration provide substantial moat; sales cycles and outcome evidence remain critical. Numeric funding is null because the company reports only more than €70M. Dedupe watch: healthcare mission.

name: Iktos
product: Integrates generative molecular design, retrosynthesis, automated chemistry and biological testing across the drug-discovery cycle.
targetCustomer: Pharmaceutical and biotechnology discovery teams
buyer: Head of medicinal chemistry, discovery R&D or business development
fundingDisplay: €15.5M Series A plus €2.5M EIC grant; cumulative equity not verified
latestRound: €2.5M EIC Accelerator grant, 2025; optional €5M investment not counted
traction: Iktos reports more than 60 collaborations and signed a 2026 multi-target Servier agreement with potential value above €1B; that figure includes contingent milestones and is not revenue.
